hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

In other words, the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector between any pair of corresponding points in the image and the pre-image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
Since line $\ell$ is *vertical*, the reflection will move each point of quadrilateral $ABCD$ *horizontally* across the line of reflection.

For example, point $A$ is $2$ units to the left of line $\ell$, so $A'$ will be $2$ units to the right of $\ell$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. A vertical line is labeled l. Quadrilateral A B C D has point A two units away from the line on the left side, point B is three units away from the line on the left side, point C is on the line, and point D is one unit away from the line on the left side. A dashed arrow points at both point A prime at which is two units away on the right side of the line and point A.

hints.content:
We can reflect each of the other vertices in the same way.



[[☃ image 1]]

We note that points $C$ and $C'$ are in the same place because $C$ was on the line of reflection.
